name: Pink Purple
lede: Pink Purple names a vivid magenta by plain modifier grammar, combining [[pink]] and [[purple]], and the xkcd 2010 crowd survey is the only dated record our sources carry for it.

sections.title: A compound, surveyed in 2010
sections.body:
The name follows the modifier pattern "pink" plus the parent hue [[purple]], describing a hue that sits between the two [1]. Our library's only dated record for this exact pairing is the 2010 xkcd online color-naming survey [2]. The same survey, and others in our library, recorded several near-twins for the same hue: [[pinky-purple]], [[pinky-purple]] and [[pale-magenta]], along with Fuchsia (Crayola) as an unrelated brand name for a close shade [3].

The nearest named colors by measured distance are [[pale-magenta]], duller, and [[pinky-purple]], also duller [4]. [[magenta]] reads more vivid; [[medium-orchid]] is duller, and [[steel-pink]] darker [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 paintings carries this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of the swatch, as photographed [5]. A hue this saturated and this far from any natural pigment is uncommon across the whole archive, so the absence fits the pattern for its family rather than marking anything unusual [5].
